SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION

[Release No. 34-106821; File No. S7-2026-26]

Order Under Section 36 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Exchange Act”)

Granting Conditional Exemptive Relief from Section 15(c)(3) of and Rule 15c3-3a, Note H

under the Exchange Act Relating to Certain Centrally Cleared U.S. Treasury Transactions

November 4, 2026.

I.     Introduction

       A.       Overview of Exemptive Order

       The Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) is granting exemptive relief

to broker-dealers from certain provisions of Note H to Item 15 of Exhibit A to Exchange Act

Rule 15c3-3 (“Rule 15c3-3a, Note H” or “Note H”) pursuant to section 36 1 of the Exchange Act.

More specifically, the Commission is granting exemptive relief from the application of Exchange

Act section 15(c)(3) 2 and Rule 15c3-3a, Note H(b)(1) and (b)(2)(i) thereunder to permit broker-

dealers to include a debit in their Rule 15c3-3a customer and proprietary securities accounts of

other broker-dealers (“PAB”) 3 reserve computations (collectively “reserve computations”) for

margin required and on deposit with a qualified clearing agency 4 resulting from transactions in

U.S. Treasury securities in customer accounts that have been cleared, settled, and novated by the

       B.      Background

       Rule 15c3-3 under the Exchange Act, the broker-dealer customer protection rule, requires

broker-dealers that hold customer cash and securities (“carrying broker-dealers”) to treat these

assets in a manner that facilitates their prompt return to the customers if the broker-dealer fails

financially. To meet this objective, Rule 15c3-3 requires a carrying broker-dealer to take two

primary steps to safeguard customer assets, which are designed to protect customers by

segregating their securities and cash from the carrying broker-dealer’s proprietary business

activities. The first step requires carrying broker-dealers to maintain physical possession or

control over customers’ fully paid and excess margin securities. 6 The second step requires that a

carrying broker-dealer maintain a reserve of cash or qualified securities (e.g., U.S. Treasury

securities) in an account at a third-party bank that is at least equal in value to the net cash owed

to customers determined by a computation pursuant to a formula set forth in Exchange Act Rule

15c3-3a, the customer reserve computation. 7 The goal of Rule 15c3-3 is to place a broker-dealer

in a position where it is able to wind down and return customer assets in an orderly self-

liquidation without the need for financial assistance.

the standards applicable to certain clearing agencies to enhance risk management practices for

                i. Gross vs. Net Customer Position Margin Requirement

       Among the conditions necessary for including customer position margin as a debit in the

reserve computations is that customer position margin must be treated in accordance with rules

that must be adopted by the qualified clearing agency. 10 Paragraph (b)(2)(i) of Note H requires

the qualified clearing agency to calculate a separate margin amount for each customer of the

for each customer on a gross, customer-by-customer basis. 11 The Commission adopted this

requirement to ensure that the risk of one customer’s positions could not be offset by the risk of

another customer’s positions in determining the amount of customer margin the broker-dealer

would need to have on deposit at the qualified clearing agency. 12 Thus, under existing Note H

II.     Discussion of Exemptive Relief

        A. Statement of Relief

        Since the Commission’s adoption of the Treasury Clearing Adopting Release, broker-

dealers undertaking implementation have raised concerns in letters and meetings with

Commission staff about the inefficiencies and costs of the gross basis requirement. 24 For

example, SIFMA stated in its Application that implementing a strict customer-by-customer

positions, margin requirements, and collateral flows to individual customers across all clearance,

Where broker-dealers elect not to fully implement the systems and processes necessary to

support gross, customer-level margining (and thus cannot use the Item 15 debit), SIFMA has

       The Commission finds that allowing the inclusion of a debit in Item 15 of the reserve

computations where a qualified clearing agency has calculated the required customer margin on

either a net, omnibus or gross, customer-by-customer basis, and the broker-dealer has delivered

the required customer margin collateral on a net, omnibus basis, when subject to the conditions

detailed below, is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, and is consistent with the

protection of investors.

       The operational complexities and challenges of the gross, customer-by-customer margin

and delivery requirements have proven greater than anticipated before broker-dealers began to

implement them. While the Commission originally adopted Note H to require posting margin on

a gross, customer-by-customer basis for customer protection, the operational complexity of the

gross calculation and delivery approach and the attendant potential negative impact for clearing

of U.S. Treasury securities transactions warrant allowing alternative margin calculation and

       This relief would also provide broker-dealers with more flexibility to efficiently

intermediate access to centrally cleared U.S. Treasury markets while preserving the customer

protection framework under Rule 15c3-3. Further, this relief would alleviate certain capital and

operational constraints that can arise through a gross, customer-by-customer margining and

delivery requirement, particularly when broker-dealers serve smaller or indirect customers,

thereby supporting broader market access, enhancing liquidity, and advancing the Commission’s

goal of promoting a deep, resilient, and inclusive U.S. Treasury market. Finally, the alternative

margin calculation and delivery approaches will support a broker-dealer’s customer facilitation

activity in U.S. Treasury clearing, particularly in light of the expansion of these activities and the

increased number of qualified clearing agencies.

       The conditions of this order, discussed below in section II.B, are designed to permit the

Item 15 debit only in circumstances that provide protections to customers consistent with the

customer protection objectives of Rules 15c3-3 and 15c3-3a without requiring a gross, customer-

by-customer calculation and collection of customer margin. For example, Rule 15c3-3 requires

broker-dealers to take steps to safeguard customer assets by segregating their securities and cash

from the carrying broker-dealer’s proprietary business activities. 30 The conditions in this order

are designed to ensure that customer margin is appropriately segregated and that a broker-dealer

cannot use customer cash and securities to finance its proprietary business activities. Further,

consistent with the conditions in Note H not exempted under this order, the conditions of this

order explicitly limit the exemption to customer margin required and on deposit with a qualified

reduce the likelihood of certain risks that may undermine the customer protection objectives of

Rule 15c3-3, including that broker-dealers may not appropriately safeguard customer cash and

securities or may improperly include debits in their customer reserve computation.

       Accordingly, after careful consideration of the Application, the Commission is issuing,

pursuant to section 36 of the Exchange Act, conditional exemptive relief to permit broker-dealers

to include an Item 15 debit in their customer reserve computation in cases where a qualified

clearing agency has calculated customer margin on either a net, omnibus or gross, customer-by-

customer basis, and the broker-dealer has delivered the margin collateral on a net, omnibus basis,

rather than on a gross, customer-by-customer basis. Further, the Commission is providing

broker-dealers with the same relief as to their PAB account holders and PAB reserve

computation under Rule 15c3-3a, subject to the same conditions. This relief will permit either:

(1) the calculation and delivery of customer margin on a net, omnibus basis, 31 or (2) the

calculation of margin on a gross, customer-by-customer basis and the delivery of margin on a

net, omnibus basis. The following discussion describes conditions of the exemptive relief

provided by this order.

       B.       Discussion of Conditions

qualified clearing agency in connection with (1) purchases and sales of U.S. Treasury securities;

and (2) U.S. Treasury securities repurchase and reverse repurchase agreements in customer

証券取引委員会（委員会）は、証券取引所法第36条［1］に基づき、ブローカー・ディーラーに対し、同法規則15c3-3の別表A、第15項の注H（規則15c3-3a注H、以下「注H」）の一部規定からの適用免除を認める。

具体的には、委員会は、証券取引所法第15条(c)(3)［2］および同法に基づく規則15c3-3a注H(b)(1)、(b)(2)(i)の適用からの免除を認める。これによりブローカー・ディーラーは、規則15c3-3aに基づく顧客勘定および他のブローカー・ディーラーの自己証券勘定（PAB）［3］の準備額計算において、適格清算機関［4］によって清算・決済・更改された顧客勘定の米国債取引に伴い要求され、同機関に預託された証拠金を控除項目に含めることができる。［文は次頁へ続く］

［1］15 U.S.C. 78mm。同法第36条(a)(1)は、公共の利益に照らして必要または適切で、投資家保護に合致する範囲で、委員会に対し、規則、規制または命令によって、あらゆる者、証券または取引、あるいはその一つ以上の区分を、条件付きまたは無条件で、同法のいずれの規定からも免除する権限を与える。

［3］17 CFR 240.15c3-3(a)(16)参照。PABは、ブローカー・ディーラー（外国のブローカー・ディーラーや、その資格で行動する外国銀行を含む）の自己証券勘定のうち、支払いと引渡し、または支払いと受渡しを同時に行う勘定を除くものを指す。口座を管理するブローカー・ディーラーの債権者の請求に劣後する勘定も含まない。

       B.      Background

       Rule 15c3-3 under the Exchange Act, the broker-dealer customer protection rule, requires

broker-dealers that hold customer cash and securities (“carrying broker-dealers”) to treat these

assets in a manner that facilitates their prompt return to the customers if the broker-dealer fails

financially. To meet this objective, Rule 15c3-3 requires a carrying broker-dealer to take two

primary steps to safeguard customer assets, which are designed to protect customers by

segregating their securities and cash from the carrying broker-dealer’s proprietary business

activities. The first step requires carrying broker-dealers to maintain physical possession or

control over customers’ fully paid and excess margin securities. 6 The second step requires that a

carrying broker-dealer maintain a reserve of cash or qualified securities (e.g., U.S. Treasury

securities) in an account at a third-party bank that is at least equal in value to the net cash owed

to customers determined by a computation pursuant to a formula set forth in Exchange Act Rule

15c3-3a, the customer reserve computation. 7 The goal of Rule 15c3-3 is to place a broker-dealer

in a position where it is able to wind down and return customer assets in an orderly self-

liquidation without the need for financial assistance.
